topics.focus: How to reduce lockout risks when changing Proxmox VE networking, without providing unsafe universal commands

sources.name: Proxmox VE official network configuration guide

facts.text: Proxmox VE uses Linux bridges for connecting guests to physical networks; bridge interfaces are often named vmbr0 or vmbr1.
The Proxmox VE graphical interface stages networking changes in /etc/network/interfaces.new rather than changing /etc/network/interfaces immediately.
With ifupdown2, the interface can apply staged network changes without restarting the entire host. This is not a guarantee that connectivity stays available.
Incorrect changes to a host's network can make it unreachable. An out-of-band management plan or console access reduces recovery risk.
The Proxmox VE documentation warns against indiscriminate use of traditional ifup and ifdown commands because they may interrupt guest traffic.
